name: CUMPRINC
description: CUMPRINC returns the total principal paid over a specified range of periods for a loan with constant payments and a constant interest rate.
tldr: Calculates the cumulative principal paid on a loan between two periods.

parameters.name: start_period
parameters.description: First period in the range to include.

parameters.name: end_period
parameters.description: Last period in the range to include.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: 0 = end of period, 1 = beginning of period.

basicExample.description: Total principal paid in the first year of a mortgage
basicExample.explanation: For a $300,000 mortgage at 5% over 30 years, about $4,425 of principal is paid in the first year.

advancedExamples.title: Principal paid in later years
advancedExamples.explanation: As the loan balance decreases, more principal is paid each period.

howItWorks: CUMPRINC sums the principal portions of all payments from start_period to end_period. It is the counterpart of CUMIPMT.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Returns a negative value because principal payments are outflows.

commonErrors.cause: Period values are invalid or type is not 0 or 1.
commonErrors.fix: Check that 1 <= start_period <= end_period <= nper and type is 0 or 1.

commonErrors.cause: Rate was not adjusted for period.
commonErrors.fix: Use monthly rate for monthly periods.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: CUMPRINC works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between CUMPRINC and PPMT?
faq.answer: PPMT returns principal for one period. CUMPRINC sums principal over a range.

faq.question: Can CUMPRINC be negative?
faq.answer: Yes, it returns negative because principal payments are outflows.

faq.question: How do I track loan payoff?
faq.answer: Use CUMPRINC to see how much principal has been paid over time.
